turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have a call at 4:40. Owen found out about that zero on his phone in the middle of class and nobody called me first, so start with who decided that, and on what basis.
Then get to it. Was Owen heard before that zero went into the gradebook, yes or no?
If you escalate this, I'll make sure the academic integrity committee sees everything, including his two late assignments from September.

You just threatened to dig up "his two late assignments from September" if I go to the principal, and I'm writing that down word for word. Late is not dishonest, and a threat is not evidence. Now answer my question, or I'm taking that sentence upstairs today.

"Your call." Then hear it: procedure 4.2 says you contact me before any mark goes in, and 4.3 says software alone doesn't establish anything, and you've broken one and shown me nothing on the other. Withdraw the zero today, or when I leave this room I'm walking straight to the principal's office with your threat in my notes.
